text:
A muscle fibre relaxes when calcium ions are pumped back into the sarcoplasmic reticulum, causing troponin-tropomyosin to block the myosin-binding sites on actin and halting cross-bridge cycling. Note that the shared claim is incorrect: skeletal muscle fibres are stimulated by motor neurons via the neuromuscular junction, not by sensory neurons bypassing it. Relaxation follows cessation of that motor signal and calcium reuptake.
CONFIDENCE: 90
